rationale: This is the final iteration, so the design raced here is the one scored on the unseen final track. The evidence favours the best raced design, not a new untested change. Iteration 10 tested base_speed 0.9 and scored 81.76, below iteration 6 (85.60, reproduced exactly in iteration 9). At 0.9, oval progress fell from 0.3425 to 0.3279, oval max_error rose from 0.0623 to 0.0651, and oval line losses rose from 0 to 0.95. That is the 'speed too slow' outcome the Evaluator named, so I am returning to base_speed 1.0. Every other field stays at the iteration 6 values: geometry (five 16 mm sensors at x = -0.05, -0.025, 0, 0.025, 0.05 m, y = 0.04 m), kp 4.0, ki 0.05, kd 0.30, weights -1, -0.5, 0, 0.5, 1, and line_loss search_left. Sensor and kd changes were rejected by iterations 7 and 8, and recovery direction did not move s-bend or slalom. Expected result: about 85.6 on the development tracks, with oval progress near 0.34 and 0 oval line losses. Unseen-track performance is uncertain, and this design is the most reliable known option. Open hypotheses for the record: oval max_error stays just above 0.06 at this speed, and s-bend and slalom keep one line loss each. Measurements requested: all ten, to confirm reproduction and show the per-track line-loss and max_error values.
